title: Hazel and the Tide
premise: Yara Halloran, a single father hiding from his family's judgment and a past scandal that cost him everything, hires Hazel Quinn—a ferry mechanic passing through town—as his fake date for the Halloran family reunion on Saltmere Island. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Hazel sees through Yara's careful invisibility, and Yara discovers Hazel is secretly gathering evidence against the ferry company's corrupt owner, who happens to be Yara's brother-in-law. When the truth of both their deceptions surfaces at the reunion, Yara must choose between protecting his family's name and testifying to what he knows. In the end, he speaks the truth, loses his family's approval but regains himself, and catches the last ferry of the season—not to leave, but to bring Hazel back before the winter crossing closes.
about_author: E. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former island ferry worker who spent a decade writing in the margins of tide tables and ticket stubs. Sterling now lives half the year in a coastal bookshop town, where the ferries still stop running every November.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Closing the bookshop on a gray October evening, Yara receives his mother's summons to the Halloran reunion—where his ex and her new husband, ferry magnate Callum Voss, will be guests of honor. The emotional beat: dread sharpened by the realization that another season of hiding has quietly become a life.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Grease on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ferry mechanic Hazel Quinn arrives in town for a two-week contract and wanders into the only lit storefront, the bookshop, to wait out a rainstorm. She and Yara argue about a novel; she buys it just to win. Emotional beat: two guarded people briefly, unexpectedly delighted.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Desperate after learning his sister plans to stage an 'intervention' about his singleness, Yara tracks Hazel down at the dock and offers to pay her to pose as his girlfriend for the reunion weekend. She laughs him off—but takes the book back to read. Emotional beat: humiliation laced with stubborn hope.

chapters.title: What Hazel Knows About Sinking Boats
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Alone in her rented room, Hazel reads the novel and studies a folder she keeps hidden: maintenance records suggesting Voss Ferries has been falsifying hull inspections. She accepts Yara's offer—for access to the reunion, where Voss will be. Emotional beat: guilt over using a kind man as cover.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over two days of 'practice dates,' Yara and Hazel build their fake history—how they met, first kiss, inside jokes—and accidentally accumulate real ones. His daughter Wren, eight and sharp-eyed, immediately likes Hazel too much. Emotional beat: the lie becoming load-bearing.

chapters.title: Crossing to Saltmere
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The ferry ride to the island, with Hazel's hand in his for the benefit of watching relatives. Yara points out landmarks of his old life, including the boathouse where his marriage ended. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into grief he thought he'd finished paying.

chapters.title: The Halloran Welcome
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The reunion begins: Yara's mother performs warmth like a hostess skill, his sister Nell probes Hazel with polite cruelty, and Callum Voss greets Yara with condescending charm. Hazel recognizes Voss from her files and nearly breaks cover. Emotional beat: performing intimacy while cataloguing an enemy.

chapters.title: Cocktails and Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At drinks, Callum corners Yara with an offer: come work for Voss Ferries, restore the family's good opinion, forget the past. Yara realizes Callum needs him more than he admits. Meanwhile Hazel charms Nell genuinely. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as forgiveness.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During dinner, Wren gets overwhelmed and hides; Hazel finds her under the dessert table and stays until she laughs. Watching them, Yara forgets the audience entirely. Later, on the porch, their rehearsed 'first kiss story' almost becomes real. Emotional beat: the fiction collapsing under its own weight.

chapters.title: What Nell Saw
chapters.summary: Nell's POV (brief interlude). Nell watches her brother laugh—really laugh—for the first time since the scandal, and feels something between relief and suspicion. She notices Hazel photographing the boathouse. Emotional beat: love expressed as surveillance.

chapters.title: The Boathouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel sneaks to the boathouse and photographs Voss's private launch—evidence of the falsified inspections—just as Yara follows her there. Cornered, she confesses why she came: her father was injured when a Voss ferry's hull failed, and the company buried it. Emotional beat: betrayal transforming into alliance.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reveals his own secret: years ago he discovered Voss's fraud and stayed silent in exchange for the settlement that let him keep Wren and open the bookshop. His invisibility was purchased. He agrees to help Hazel—if she never tells Wren what he did. Emotional beat: shame offered like a confession.

chapters.title: Stolen Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Back on the mainland, the fake relationship dissolves into a real one: late nights in the bookshop, Hazel teaching Wren knots, Yara fixing Hazel's motorcycle badly. But Hazel's contract ends soon, and the last ferry of the season looms. Emotional beat: happiness with an expiration date.

chapters.title: Nell's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell confronts Yara: she knows Hazel was paid, has seen the transfer. She gives him a choice—end it quietly or she tells their mother and Callum. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized, a sister convinced she's protecting him.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Yara compile the evidence: inspection records, the boathouse photos, and Yara's memory of the original documents. They need one more piece—the master manifest locked in Voss's island office during the reunion's final night. Emotional beat: fear converted into resolve.

chapters.title: Everything Breaks at Once
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Nell exposes Hazel at a family dinner; Yara's mother demands he choose the family or 'that woman.' Wren overhears that Hazel was paid and runs. Yara, publicly humiliated, watches Hazel walk out rather than let Wren hear worse. Emotional beat: the lie detonating, taking the truth with it.

chapters.title: Low Tide, No Excuses
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Packing to leave, Hazel finds Wren waiting at her door—not angry, but asking if any of it was real. Hazel can't lie to her. She leaves the evidence file with Wren's babysitter addressed to Yara and books nothing. Emotional beat: honesty as the only gift left to give.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reading Hazel's file, Yara understands the full scope of Voss's fraud—and that silence now makes him complicit in future wrecks. He calls Nell, tells her everything including his own old bargain, and asks for the office key she holds as Voss's wife. Emotional beat: choosing truth over the family's fragile peace.

chapters.title: Reunion, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. At the reunion's final gala, Yara takes the microphone instead of accepting Callum's toast, presenting the manifest and confessing his own years of silence. Nell stands and confirms it. Voss's composure cracks; the maritime authority, tipped by Hazel, is already waiting at the dock. Emotional beat: public ruin as rebirth.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Fallout: his mother cuts contact, Nell wavers between fury and gratitude, and the bookshop fills with quiet support from townsfolk. Yara lets Wren decide about Hazel; Wren says Hazel never lied to her. Yara writes a letter he has no address for. Emotional beat: grief that finally feels clean.

chapters.title: Before the Winter Crossing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the mainland, Hazel learns Voss has been suspended pending investigation and her father's case reopened. She intends to leave quietly—but Wren's letter reaches her via the ferry crew. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as ordinary mail.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Tide
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV. On the last day of the season, Yara boards the final ferry not to flee but to meet it halfway—Hazel is aboard, having decided the tide could carry her back. On the dock, no audience, no pretense, they begin again honestly. Epilogue beat: spring comes early to the bookshop.
